apod_title: Hubble: Decagon Around Saturn's South Pole
label: namecode - HUBBLE.DECAGON | 84.261
prompt: Cinematic dark monochrome generative art inspired by Hubble: Decagon Around Saturn's South Pole. Why are Saturn’s poles geometric? Saturn’s North Pole has been known to be surrounded by a hexagonal (6 sides) cloud since discovery in 1987 in data taken by NASA’s Voyager spacecrafts, which quickly Rendered as fine white particles and light filaments on a pure black background, volumetric, dramatic, monochrome white on black, lots of negative space, high detail.
